title: The Social Construction of Reality
text:
Sociologists emphasize that much of what is accepted as objective reality is, in fact, a product of cultural agreement and shared interpretation. This concept suggests that knowledge and meaning are not simply derived from an external world but are built through ongoing social interactions.

The processes by which groups define concepts such as 'gender,' 'money,' or 'national identity' illustrate this mechanism. Because consensus dictates the operational rules for these constructs, their disappearance would fundamentally alter social structure, even if physical evidence of them remained.
